headline: GOLD AND SILVER HIT 52-WEEK LOWS BUT JUNIOR MINERS KEEP DRILLING — Nov 22 Morning Brief: TSX-V And ASX Hold On Strong Results
snippet: Mining Stock Daily's November 22 morning briefing covers the defining tension of the current junior mining market: gold and silver trading at 52-week lows — gold at approximately $3,540 per ounce, down 36% from January's $5,588 all-time high, and silver near $41.25 — while TSX-V and ASX-listed junior exploration companies continue to publish meaningful drill results on funded 2026 programs. The briefing notes that the disconnect between deteriorating metal prices and strong operational news creates the kind of setup that historically precedes sharp re-ratings: programs funded at higher metals prices in 2025–2026 are delivering discovery-stage results into a weaker equity environment, leaving well-managed juniors fundamentally de-risked but equity-price punished. For self-directed retail investors trying to separate price-driven fear from operational reality, the morning brief's weekly roundup provides context for what the correction is — and what it is not — ahead of the Thanksgiving-week market lull.

headline: CABRAL GOLD TRIPLES CUIÚ CUIÚ RESOURCE TO 3.51M OZ IN BRAZIL — Majority Inferred, But PEA Advances As Cash Flow Covers Next Phase
snippet: Cabral Gold's Cuiú Cuiú gold project in Brazil recorded a resource that roughly tripled to 3.51 million ounces — a substantial increase in total inventory, though Discovery Alert's analysis flags that the majority of the ounces are classified as inferred rather than indicated or measured. The resource growth reflects continued drilling at Cuiú Cuiú, which is Cabral's flagship project in Pará state, Brazil, and sets the foundation for a Preliminary Economic Assessment now being advanced. Management says that Phase 1 cash flow from the project is expected to fund both exploration and the PEA without requiring additional dilutive equity raises — a significant point for investors in the current environment where balance sheet integrity is under intense scrutiny. For TSX-listed junior gold investors, the 3.51Moz total is headline-grabbing, but the inferred classification caveat matters: inferred resources carry higher geological uncertainty and cannot be used as the basis for production or feasibility studies. The transition from inferred to indicated through infill drilling will determine whether Cuiú Cuiú's resource quantity translates into robust project economics at a time when gold's price correction is compressing junior valuations globally.

headline: SILVER NORTH EXTENDS HALDANE MAIN FAULT 100 METRES WITH 722 g/t SILVER — Yukon Discovery Grows With 16 More Holes Still Pending
snippet: Silver North Resources (TSX-V: SNAG) reported step-out drilling at its Haldane silver project in the Keno Hill district of Yukon extended Main Fault mineralization approximately 100 metres further in the southwestern direction, with new holes returning grades reaching 722 g/t silver — adding discovery footprint to a project that completed its largest-ever drill program in October, with 24 holes totaling 6,169 metres. The company notes that 16 additional drill holes from the 2026 program are still pending assay, maintaining investor interest in a continued discovery expansion story heading into year-end. Silver's sharp correction — spot price near $41.25, down approximately 28% over the past 30 days and at 52-week lows — adds both risk and opportunity context for Haldane investors: in-the-ground silver discovery economics are improving while equity compression means the market has not yet rewarded the exploration success. The Keno Hill district, home to some of the world's highest-grade historical silver mines and currently producing silver from Hecla Mining's nearby operations, provides district validation for Haldane's exploration thesis at a moment when silver's physical-equity divergence is as wide as it has been in several years.

headline: OMAI GOLD ANNOUNCES 12 MORE DRILL HOLES FROM WENOT DEPOSIT IN GUYANA — Flagship 50,000-Metre Program Advances At World-Class Gold Project
snippet: Omai Gold Mines Corp. (TSX-V: OMG) released assay results from an additional 12 diamond drill holes totalling 6,913 metres at its Wenot deposit — the core of the Omai Gold Project in Guyana — continuing the advance of a 50,000-metre, multi-rig drilling program that has consistently returned high-grade gold mineralization in 2026. The Omai project sits on the site of the former Omai Mine, one of the largest gold mines in South American history, operated by Cambior and Golden Star Resources before its closure in 2005; modern exploration by Omai Gold is demonstrating that the deposit remains open in multiple directions and contains high-grade zones amenable to resource expansion. Guyana's mining jurisdiction has steadily improved, with government infrastructure investment, transparent royalty structures, and ExxonMobil-driven economic growth making it a more attractive exploration address than its historical perception. For TSX-V investors evaluating global gold exploration exposure, Omai's consistent drill result cadence and project scale — with a resource update expected as the 50,000-metre program concludes — represent the type of systematic, properly funded discovery-expansion story that tends to attract institutional attention regardless of near-term gold price volatility.

headline: VAL-D'OR MINING AND ELDORADO GOLD JV COMPLETE 25-HOLE PERESTROIKA PROGRAM — 7.30m At 2.92 g/t Au Extends Quebec Gold System
snippet: Val-D'Or Mining (TSX-V: VZZ) and its 70/30 joint venture with Eldorado Gold (TSX/NYSE: ELD) completed a 25-hole, 12,477-metre diamond drill program at the Perestroika Prospect in the prolific Val-d'Or gold camp of Quebec, with results including a best intersection of 7.30 metres grading 2.92 g/t gold. The JV structure — with Eldorado Gold holding a 30% interest — is strategically notable: Eldorado is a mid-tier gold producer with operating mines in Turkey, Greece, and Canada, and its sustained participation in an early-stage Quebec exploration program signals continued belief in the Val-d'Or district's exploration potential. While the 7.30m at 2.92 g/t intersection is not high-grade by Abitibi-Témiscamingue standards — which has historically produced some of the world's richest gold veins — the program completion and consistent mineralization across 25 holes provides geological data to plan follow-up drilling targeting higher-grade feeder structures. The Val-d'Or camp remains one of Canada's most explored and best-understood gold districts, with active projects from Agnico Eagle, Monarch Mining, and several TSX-V juniors providing validation and optionality on further consolidation.

headline: GENESIS AND VAULT COMPLETE $12.6B AUSTRALIAN GOLD MEGA-MERGER — New Entity To Produce 600K–700K Oz Annually; WA Court Clears Deal
snippet: Genesis Minerals (ASX: GMD) and Vault Minerals (ASX: VAU) are completing their landmark Australian gold mega-merger in November 2026, following Western Australian Supreme Court approval of the scheme and the absence of a competing bid from Regis Resources (which had previously signed a merger agreement with Vault before Genesis submitted its superior proposal in July). The combined company — valued at approximately A$12.6 billion — merges Genesis's producing Leonora Operations with Vault's Murchison and other WA gold assets to create an entity targeting 600,000 to 700,000 ounces of gold production annually, with management estimating approximately A$2.0 billion in post-tax undiscounted synergies. Genesis CEO Matt Nixon will lead the combined group and the new board will draw directors from both legacy entities. For ASX and TSX-listed gold investors, the Genesis-Vault transaction is the capstone consolidation deal in a year that saw significant Australian gold M&A activity, following Eldorado/Foran, Altius/TNR, and Freeport/TDG. The merger creates a new Australian gold major with the production profile, balance sheet, and operating leverage to absorb gold price volatility more effectively than standalone mid-tier operators, and potentially attracts institutional funds mandated to hold major mining equity.

headline: CHINA ISSUES THREE COPPER SCRAP POLICIES IN ONE MONTH — SMM: Recycled Supply Surge Could Soften Any Refined Copper Price Recovery
snippet: Shanghai Metals Market's November 22 analysis examines the significance of three Chinese government policy documents on copper scrap issued in rapid succession in early-to-mid November 2026 — a policy cluster that SMM argues is reshaping the competitive dynamics between China's recycled copper sector and primary refined copper production. The policies collectively aim to accelerate domestic copper scrap collection, processing, and utilization, targeting the 'circular economy' mandates that Beijing has embedded in its critical minerals strategy. For the global copper market, the SMM analysis identifies a potential medium-term implication that juniors should understand: if China successfully scales up copper scrap recycling, the increment of refined copper demand growth needed to sustain elevated LME prices may be partly absorbed by scrap rather than primary mine production. This does not alter the structural long-term deficit thesis — which is driven by electrification, EVs, and AI data centre infrastructure — but it represents a supply-side wildcard that could moderate the speed of copper price recovery from November's bear market lows. Junior copper investors watching the LME price for signals about when to add to positions should track Chinese scrap utilization rates alongside the Yangshan import premium and LME inventory data as leading indicators.

headline: ZACKS: 4 GOLD MINING STOCKS POSITIONED TO WEATHER INDUSTRY HEADWINDS — Fury Gold, B2Gold, Gold Royalty Among Names As Sector Tests Multi-Month Lows
snippet: Zacks Investment Research identifies four gold mining stocks — including Fury Gold Mines, B2Gold, Gold Royalty Corp., and Newmont — as most likely to hold up against the current industry headwinds: gold price correction, cost inflation, and macro-driven equity de-risking that has pushed even quality producers to multi-month valuation lows. The analysis applies Zacks's earnings estimate methodology, noting that Newmont's 2026 earnings are projected to grow approximately 33% year over year despite near-term price pressure, and frames royalty and streaming companies as offering superior downside protection because their cost structures do not scale with mining inflation the way operating mine costs do. For TSX-V retail investors with heavy junior exploration exposure, the Zacks framework offers a useful complement: understanding which mid-tier and large-cap operators are resilient helps calibrate risk — companies that Zacks sees as well-insulated from the correction are more likely to remain active exploration JV partners, royalty purchasers, and strategic acquirers. The B2Gold and Gold Royalty inclusions are of particular relevance to TSX-V investors given both companies' active Canadian and international development-stage project exposure.
